title: Trump heads to Ohio to support Husted in close Senate race
summary:
President Donald Trump was heading to Ohio on Saturday, October 3, 2026, for a campaign rally near Dayton. He wanted to support Republicans before the November 3 elections. Senator Jon Husted faces Democrat Sherrod Brown in a close race.

Husted was chosen to fill JD Vance’s Senate seat when Vance became vice president. Now Husted wants to win the seat in an election. Brown served three terms in the Senate. He wants to return after losing to Republican Bernie Moreno two years ago.

This race could help decide which party controls the Senate. Democrats see Ohio as important to winning a majority, or more than half the seats. Senator Tim Scott, who leads the Senate Republicans’ campaign committee, said this week that the race was about even.

The economy is a big issue. Trump says it is doing better than voters think. But polls show Americans are unhappy with how he handles it. People near Dayton worry about living costs. Nearly 1,400 workers recently lost jobs at a truck factory in nearby Springfield.

The candidates also disagree about data centers. These buildings hold computers for services like artificial intelligence (AI). Some voters worry about electricity prices, farmland and water supplies.

Brown criticized Husted’s work to bring data centers to Ohio, including tax breaks for technology companies. Scott said Husted supports careful development and would oppose a project if the community did not want it. Trump supports data centers. He says they help the United States compete with China in AI.

Ohio’s governor race is also close. Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a business owner and former presidential candidate, faces Democrat Dr. Amy Acton, Ohio’s former health director. Ramaswamy has raised much more money, but the race remains competitive with weeks before voting day.
why_it_matters: Ohio’s close Senate race could help decide which party controls the Senate. The campaigns also discuss living costs and how data centers could affect communities.
